paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Christ did what no priest, no goat and no yearly routine could ever finish. He is the mediator of a new covenant, and He died so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance (Hebrews 9:15). Even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood, and "without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness" (Hebrews 9:18, 22). That's not a rule to be scared of. It tells you how seriously forgiveness was taken, and how much it cost.

Now watch the contrast, because it's the heart of this passage. The high priest went in every year with blood that was not his own, but Christ "has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself" (Hebrews 9:25-26). Once! One time, and it was enough! No second batch, no touch-ups, no "let me just run it through the oven again." Even I, a stamper with soft edges and blurry lines, know that when a thing is truly finished, you stop pressing on it. And Christ is in heaven right now, appearing on our behalf in the presence of God (Hebrews 9:24).

So what do you do with that, baker? You rest in it, and you wait with eager hearts. Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many, and He "will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him" (Hebrews 9:28). That's the whole reason my ovens stay ready. I don't know the day, and nobody does (Matthew 24:36), so I just keep baking, grateful and watching. Friend, you can do the same.
